## Canary's actual state — and a correction

I need to correct what I told you earlier. When I reported the canary "converged", I had read **PR 121's branch**, not the canary's `main`. The canary itself has not converged:

- `main` is still **engine 4**, declaring `core` and `grow_with_claudinite`, with the old mount directories.
- [PR 121](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/pull/121) is open, labelled **`needs-human`**, `mergeable_state: unstable`, body: *"apply-stage — 2 withheld workflow file(s) staged under `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`"*.

That's the designed credential lane, not a fault: the pack flow computes the scheduler/executor workflow content but can't push under `.github/workflows/` with the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so it withholds those paths for a session that can write them. The update is parked awaiting that, which is why `main` never moved.

So my earlier "the member converged" was wrong in an important way — the *delivery* converged on a branch; the *member* did not. The evidence about the renames still holds, because it came from the delivered tree, but it was never live on the canary.

## Which repo I chose, and why

The canary is now doubly awkward as a test: it has a stale pre-fix PR open, and it's parked on an apply stage. So I picked a **real member instead — `missingbulb/LaughCounter`** — checked first that it's genuinely pre-rename:

```
engineVersion: 4
packs: [... "grow_with_claudinite", ... "core"]
packVersions: { "core": 6, "grow_with_claudinite": 6, ... }
```

Sitting at engine 4 means its gap contains **both** records — v5 (mount move + version keys) and v6 (the structural declaration rewrite) — so one run exercises the whole thing end to end, including the half that was broken. It also has the fewest packs of the candidates, so the read is least confounded. Scheduler dispatched with `wake: update`.

> ⚠️ Still open: LaughCounter's forced update is running; I'll read its declaration, stamp and mount back to confirm the `packs` array converges this time. The canary's [PR 121](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/pull/121) is stale (pre-fix canon) and parked on `needs-human` — I'd suggest closing it and re-forcing rather than completing its apply stage, but that's your call and I haven't touched it.

input.title: The stamp write carries a renamed pack's old packVersions key forward, so both spellings live in the stamp forever
input.body:
Found by forcing a real member (`missingbulb/LaughCounter`) through the engine 4 → 6 gap after #1042 and reading its `main` back.

## What is wrong

The declaration's `packs` array converged correctly — #1042's structural op works, local packs untouched:

```
packs: ["basics", "barriers", "claudinite-growth", "tidy-repo", "github-actions",
        "local/on-device-privacy", "local/macos-audio", "local/laughcounter",
        "claude-code-web-users-support", "claudinite-lifecycle"]
```

The stamp did not:

```
packVersions: { "basics": 7, "barriers": 2, "git-github": 4,
                "grow_with_claudinite": 6,          ← stale
                "tidy-repo": 5, "github-actions": 4,
                "claude-code-web-users-support": 2,
                "core": 6,                          ← stale
                "claudinite-lifecycle": 8, "claudinite-growth": 7 }
```

Both spellings, permanently.

## Cause — mine, in #1042

`canonicalPackVersions` is applied when the stamp is **read**, so a version under an old key is never mistaken for "never installed". The **write** at `updates/pack-update.mjs` spread the raw keys straight back:

```js
const packVersions = { ...(next.claudinite?.packVersions ?? {}) };
for (const p of plan) if (p.to !== null) packVersions[p.id] = p.to;
```

The v5 record used to clean this up textually (`/"core"(\s*:)/`) — a key match, unaffected by the nested-array bug that broke its sibling patterns. When #1042 removed that whole `rewrite` block as broken, it removed the half that worked. The canary's pre-#1042 run shows only the new keys; LaughCounter's post-#1042 run shows both.

## Impact

No misbehaviour: `canonicalPackVersions` prefers today's spelling when both keys are present, so every read resolves to `claudinite-lifecycle: 8`. What it costs is the same thing the packs-array bug cost — the rename can never be called finished, because the retirement test for `renamed-packs.mjs` is "no member's declaration **and no member's stamped packVersions** still carries the old spelling". A stale key also reads as a pack nobody has heard of to anything enumerating the stamp.

## Fix

Canonicalize on the way out as well as in, at the stamp write in `updates/pack-update.mjs` and its counterpart in `updates/install.mjs`.

**No new record and no engine version bump.** The update flows run from a fresh canon clone rather than the member's mount, so a fix here reaches every member on its next update run regardless of the version it is stamped at. A member that is fully current keeps the residue until its next pack bump moves the stamp at all — benign, and self-clearing.

input.body:
Closes #1046. Follow-up to #1042, found the same way — by forcing a real member and reading its `main` back rather than trusting a green run.

## What the forced run showed

`missingbulb/LaughCounter`, engine 4 → 6, [PR 234](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/pull/234), merged. The declaration converged exactly as #1042 intended:

```
packs: ["basics", "barriers", "claudinite-growth", "tidy-repo", "github-actions",
        "local/on-device-privacy", "local/macos-audio", "local/laughcounter",
        "claude-code-web-users-support", "claudinite-lifecycle"]
```

Local packs untouched, order preserved, mount directories moved, contract doc in `claudinite-growth/`. The stamp did not:

```
"grow_with_claudinite": 6, ... "core": 6, "claudinite-lifecycle": 8, "claudinite-growth": 7
```

## Cause

Mine, in #1042. `canonicalPackVersions` runs when the stamp is read; the write spread the raw keys back. The v5 record used to clear them textually — a bare `"core":` key match, unaffected by the nested-array bug that broke its sibling patterns — and #1042 removed that whole `rewrite` block as broken, taking the half that worked with it. The canary's pre-#1042 run shows only new keys; LaughCounter's post-#1042 run shows both.

## Fix

Canonicalize at the stamp write too, in `updates/pack-update.mjs` and `updates/install.mjs`.

**No record, no engine version bump** — and so no canary rehearsal gate. The update flows run from a fresh canon clone rather than the member's mount, so this reaches every member on its next update run whatever version it is stamped at. A fully-current member keeps the residue until its next pack bump moves the stamp at all: benign, and self-clearing.

## Impact of the bug

No misbehaviour — reads prefer today's spelling when both keys are present. What it cost is that the rename could never be called finished: the retirement test for `renamed-packs.mjs` is "no member's declaration **and no member's stamped `packVersions`** still carries the old spelling", and this guaranteed the second half stayed false forever.

## Verification

- New assertion runs the flow's own stamp expression over a stamp holding both spellings; watched failing with `canonicalPackVersions` stubbed to identity.
- Full suite **2146 passing**, `check_the_world` 0 blocking, `check_the_work` exits 0.
- End-to-end confirmation is a forced run *after* this merges — the canary is still at engine 4 and is the natural vehicle.

[#1042](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1042) merged. Here's where everything stands.

## Canary's current state

**Not converged.** `main` is still engine 4, declaring `core`/`grow_with_claudinite`, old mount dirs. [PR 121](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/pull/121) is open, `needs-human`, parked on *"apply-stage — 2 withheld workflow file(s)"* — the designed credential lane, since the Action's token can't push `.github/workflows/`. It's also stale now: it was cut from pre-#1042 canon, so it carries the broken declaration half.

## The repo I chose, and what it proved

**`missingbulb/LaughCounter`** — picked because it was genuinely pre-rename at engine 4, so its gap held *both* records, and it has the fewest packs of the candidates. [PR 234](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/pull/234) ran engine 4 → 6 and is **merged**, so this is a live member's `main`, not a branch:

| | result |
|---|---|
| `packs` array | `claudinite-lifecycle`, `claudinite-growth` ✅ — the #1042 fix working in the field |
| local packs | `local/on-device-privacy`, `local/macos-audio`, `local/laughcounter` untouched ✅ |
| mount dirs | old gone, renamed present ✅ |
| contract doc | `claudinite-growth/scheduled-tasks.md` ✅ |
| `engineVersion` | 6 ✅ |
| `packVersions` | `core: 6` **and** `claudinite-lifecycle: 8` ❌ |

## The second defect, also mine

The stamp write spread raw keys back, so both spellings persist. #1042 removed the v5 record's whole `rewrite` block as broken — but its `packVersions` key patterns were the one part that *worked* (a bare `"core":` match doesn't hit the nested-array bug). No misbehaviour, since reads prefer today's spelling; the cost is that the aliases could never be retired, because the retirement test explicitly includes stamped `packVersions`.

Fixed in [#1047](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1047) ([#1046](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1046)) — canonicalize on write in `updates/pack-update.mjs` and `updates/install.mjs`. **No record and no engine bump**: the flows run from a fresh canon clone, so it reaches every member on its next update at any stamped version.

The pattern worth naming: both defects were invisible to a green run and to my own fixtures, and both fell out immediately from forcing a real member and reading its artifacts back. That's now twice.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#1047](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1047) awaiting review — not merged. After it lands, forcing the canary is the clean end-to-end check (it's still at engine 4, so it exercises everything at once); its stale [PR 121](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/pull/121) should be closed first rather than have its apply stage completed — your call, I haven't touched it.
